title: TD Securities Women at TD 2026–2027 University Mentorship Program for Undergraduate Women in Canada
summary: The TD Securities Women at TD University Mentorship Program 2026–2027 is a career-development and mentorship opportunity designed to encourage undergraduate women to explore careers in capital markets and learn more about opportunities within TD Securities. The program provides selected students with access to one-on-one mentorship with TD Securities leaders , group events, networking opportunities, job-shadowing experiences, and exposure to different areas of the capital markets industry. It is particularly designed for undergraduate students in their first or second year of university who are interested in building a future career in capital markets. Successful participants will take part in a structured six-month mentorship experience running approximately from October 2026 to April 2027 . About TD Securities TD Securities is the capital markets division of TD Bank and provides a broad range of financial products and services to corporate, government, and institutional clients. Its areas of activity include: Investment Banking Corporate Banking Capital Markets Interest Rate Products Currency Products Derivative Products Debt and equity underwriting and distribution Strategic mergers and acquisitions advice Trading and investment services Through its global operations, TD Securities works with clients on financial and strategic needs while providing students and early-career professionals with opportunities to learn about the financial services industry. The Women at TD University Mentorship Program is designed to give undergraduate students an opportunity to gain firsthand insight into this environment before making important decisions about their future careers. What Is the TD Securities University Mentorship Program? The TD Securities University Mentorship Program (UMP) is an initiative of the TD Securities Women at TD committee. Its primary purpose is to encourage women at the university level to explore the world of capital markets and consider pursuing careers in this area. Rather than being a traditional paid employment position, the program focuses on: Career exploration Professional mentorship Networking Leadership development Exposure to capital markets Understanding career paths within TD Securities Preparation for future co-op and graduate opportunities Selected students will be paired with TD Securities mentors who can provide guidance based on their professional experience. The program can therefore help participants better understand what working in capital markets is like and what steps they can take during university to position themselves for future opportunities. TD Securities Women at TD Mentorship Program 2026–2027 Benefits Participants can gain several valuable professional and career-development benefits throughout the six-month program. 1. One-on-One Mentorship Each selected mentee will be matched with a TD Securities mentor. The mentor may be either a woman or a man working within TD Securities. This relationship provides students with an opportunity to ask questions, seek career advice, discuss professional goals, and learn from someone with experience in the financial services industry. 2. Exposure to Capital Markets Careers The program is specifically designed for students who want to learn more about careers in capital markets. Participants can gain a better understanding of the different roles, teams, and career paths available within the industry. This can be particularly valuable for students who are still deciding which area of finance they may want to pursue. 3. Networking Opportunities Participants can develop professional relationships with TD Securities employees and other students. Networking opportunities may help students learn about: Different career paths Recruitment processes University-to-work transitions Co-op opportunities Graduate employment opportunities Skills required in capital markets 4. Trading Floor Experience Group events may provide participants with an opportunity to meet professionals from different product groups and tour the trading floor . This can give students firsthand exposure to the environment in which capital markets professionals work. 5. Job Shadowing Mentees may have opportunities to participate in job-shadowing experiences across various TD Securities groups. Job shadowing can help students understand what professionals actually do in different areas of the organization. 6. Career Guidance Participants can seek advice from TD Securities personnel about building a career in capital markets. This can help students make more informed decisions about: Academic choices Extracurricular activities Professional development Networking Internships and co-op positions Long-term career planning 7. Exposure to TD s Workplace Culture The program can also give participants an opportunity to experience TD s diverse and inclusive culture firsthand. This provides students with insight into the organization s working environment and professional expectations. 8. Potential Future Opportunities Participation in the mentorship program may help students become more familiar with future opportunities at TD Securities, including potential summer co-op and post-graduate opportunities. However, participation does not guarantee future employment or a paid position with TD Securities . Mentorship Program Structure The 2026–2027 program will select undergraduate students from various Canadian universities. Approximately: 10–15 first-year students will be accepted. 15–20 second-year students will be accepted. Selected participants will enter a structured mentoring relationship lasting approximately six months , from October 2026 to April 2027 . The formal mentorship relationship will conclude at the end of the six-month period. However, TD Securities encourages mentors and mentees to remain in contact after the formal program ends if both parties wish to continue the relationship. Monthly Commitment Applicants must be prepared to commit sufficient time and energy to the program. Participants are expected to confirm their availability for: Two one-on-one mentorship sessions per month One group event per month Applicants should therefore ensure that their academic and extracurricular schedules allow them to participate consistently. Who Is Eligible for the TD Securities Women at TD University Mentorship Program? The program has specific eligibility requirements. Applicants must meet the following criteria: 1. First- or Second-Year Undergraduate Student Applicants must currently be enrolled in their first or second year of undergraduate studies at a Canadian university. The program is intended for students graduating in: Spring 2028 , or Spring 2029 2. Identifies as a Woman The opportunity is specifically intended for undergraduate students who identify as women, including transgender women . 3. Interest in Capital Markets Applicants should have a genuine interest in pursuing a career in capital markets and an interest in TD Securities. Applicants should therefore demonstrate that they have considered why capital markets appeals to them and how the mentorship program could support their career development. 4. Strong Academic Record Applicants must demonstrate strong academic performance. Academic records will be evidenced through the submission of an official or appropriate university transcript as part of the application. 5. Leadership Skills Applicants should demonstrate leadership ability. Leadership does not necessarily have to come from formal employment. Examples may include involvement in: University clubs Student organizations Sports Extracurricular activities Community activities Other leadership initiatives Students should be able to demonstrate how they have taken initiative, influenced others, contributed to a team, or taken responsibility for achieving a goal. 6. Commitment to the Program Applicants must be prepared to dedicate the necessary time and effort to participate in the mentorship program. The monthly commitment includes two one-on-one mentorship sessions and one group event. Who Cannot Apply? Students should pay particular attention to the program s year-of-study requirements. The opportunity is not designed for: Students outside their first or second year of undergraduate study Students graduating outside the specified 2028 or 2029 graduation timelines Students who do not identify as women Students without an interest in capital markets Students unable to commit the required time to the program There is also an important restriction for returning participants. If a student previously participated in the University Mentorship Program as a first-year student, they are not eligible to participate again as a second-year student. What Documents Are Required? Applicants must submit several materials as part of their application. The required application materials include: Resume Transcript Availability confirmation Essay submission Applicants should make sure that all required documents are uploaded in the appropriate attachment section of the application. TD specifically states that applicants should submit all required documentation through the attachments section of the application process where the resume is uploaded . Essay Requirements Applicants are required to submit written responses as part of the application. The essay component contains two parts. Essay Question: Choose One Applicants must answer one of the following questions in a maximum of 400 words : Option A: Describe an experience that has shaped you as a leader. Option B: What experience made you interested in a career in capital markets? Applicants should choose the question that allows them to provide the strongest and most authentic response. For the leadership question, applicants could discuss an experience that demonstrates initiative, responsibility, teamwork, problem-solving, resilience, or the ability to influence others. For the capital markets question, applicants should explain what sparked their interest and how that experience influenced their career aspirations. Mentorship Goals and Expectations Applicants must also answer the following question in a maximum of 100 words : What are your goals and expectations of the mentoring program? A strong response should clearly explain what the applicant hopes to learn, the type of guidance they are seeking, and how the mentorship experience connects with their academic and professional goals. Application Process Students interested in applying should prepare all required documents before beginning the application. The application process requires applicants to provide: A current resume Their university transcript Confirmation of their availability Their required essay responses Their name and program of study Applicants should ensure that all documents are attached correctly before submitting the application. Application Deadline The official application deadline stated in the opportunity is: 11:59 PM EST on Sunday, September 27, 2026. Applicants are strongly encouraged to submit their applications before the deadline rather than waiting until the final hours. The job posting page currently displays an end date of September 28, 2026 , while the detailed application instructions specify 11:59 PM EST on September 27, 2026 . Applicants should therefore treat September 27, 2026 at 11:59 PM EST as the operative deadline. Is the TD Mentorship Program Paid? No. The TD Securities University Mentorship Program is explicitly described as unpaid . The purpose of the program is learning, mentorship, career development, and networking rather than paid employment. Although participation may potentially lead to future paid opportunities with TD Securities, TD does not guarantee that participation will result in employment, a co-op position, or another paid opportunity . Applicants should therefore view the program primarily as a professional development and networking opportunity. Selection and Interview Process TD Securities will review applications submitted by interested students. Only qualified candidates selected for further consideration will be contacted for an interview. The organization states that it will make efforts to communicate outcomes to applicants by email or phone. Applicants should therefore monitor the contact information provided in their application after submitting their materials. Why This Mentorship Opportunity Matters For undergraduate students interested in finance, capital markets, investment banking, trading, corporate banking, or related fields, gaining exposure to professionals early in university can be valuable. Many students begin university without a clear understanding of the different career paths available in financial services. A structured mentorship program can help bridge that knowledge gap by connecting students directly with professionals. Through the TD Securities program, participants can learn about the industry while they still have time to develop relevant academic, extracurricular, networking, and professional experiences before graduation. The opportunity may be particularly useful for students who want to understand what capital markets careers look like in practice rather than relying solely on classroom learning. What Applicants Should Highlight Students preparing their applications should consider demonstrating the following qualities: Genuine interest in capital markets Strong academic performance Leadership experience Initiative Teamwork Curiosity Communication skills Commitment to professional development Clear career aspirations Willingness to learn from mentors Ability to commit to the program s schedule The application should provide evidence rather than simply listing these qualities. For example, instead of simply stating that an applicant is a leader, the essay could describe a specific situation in which the applicant took responsibility, faced a challenge, made decisions, and achieved an outcome. About TD Bank TD is one of the major financial institutions in North America, serving more than 27 million households and businesses in Canada, the United States, and other markets. The organization has more than 95,000 employees and operates across a broad range of financial services. TD emphasizes career development, training, mentorship, inclusion, and opportunities for employees to develop their skills. The organization s stated values include Impact, Growth, and a Culture of Care , reflecting its focus on supporting customers, colleagues, and communities. Diversity, Equity and Inclusion TD states that it is committed to creating an inclusive workplace in which employees can bring their authentic selves to work and have equitable opportunities to grow. The Women at TD mentorship initiative forms part of this broader commitment to supporting diverse perspectives and encouraging women to explore careers in areas such as capital markets. Important Information for Applicants Before applying, prospective candidates should carefully review the following points: The program is for first- and second-year undergraduate students . Applicants must identify as women, including transgender women . Applicants must be enrolled at a Canadian university . Applicants should be graduating in spring 2028 or 2029 . Applicants should have a strong academic record . Applicants should demonstrate leadership skills . Applicants must have an interest in capital markets and TD Securities . Participation is unpaid . Participants must commit to two one-on-one mentorship sessions and one group event each month . The formal mentorship period is approximately October 2026 to April 2027 . Applicants must submit a resume and transcript . Applicants must complete the required essay responses . Previous first-year participants cannot participate again as second-year students. Future employment or paid opportunities are not guaranteed . The stated application deadline is 11:59 PM EST on September 27, 2026 . Conclusion The TD Securities Women at TD 2026–2027 University Mentorship Program offers eligible undergraduate women an opportunity to gain early exposure to the capital markets industry while building professional relationships with TD Securities leaders. Through structured mentorship, networking, job-shadowing opportunities, trading-floor exposure, group events, and career guidance, participants can develop a clearer understanding of capital markets and begin preparing for future co-op and graduate career opportunities. For eligible first- and second-year undergraduate students in Canada who are academically strong, demonstrate leadership, and are genuinely interested in capital markets, this program can provide valuable professional exposure well before graduation. Interested students should prepare their resume, transcript, availability confirmation, and essay responses carefully and submit their complete application by 11:59 PM EST on September 27, 2026 . title: Humanity AI Open Call 2026 | Grants of Up to $1 Million for Community-Led AI Initiatives
summary: Humanity AI has launched a first-of-its-kind Open Call for Proposals seeking community-led efforts that shape how artificial intelligence is built, governed, and used for the common good. The initiative comes at a time of growing public concern about the impact of AI on people s lives, jobs, and communities. Humanity AI is particularly interested in supporting communities that are not simply being consulted about AI but are actively setting the agenda and leading efforts to determine how AI affects them. The Open Call will provide grants ranging from $75,000 to $1,000,000 , with applicants able to propose projects lasting up to three years. About the Humanity AI Open Call The Humanity AI Open Call is designed to support community-led work addressing the social, economic, cultural, and technological implications of artificial intelligence. The initiative seeks applications from communities and organizations where those most affected by technological change are defining the goals, shaping the approach, and driving the work. This includes communities of: Workers Artists Students Educators Writers Scholars Cultural heritage workers Other communities working in the humanities and culture Humanity AI is also actively seeking applicants who may not traditionally have considered themselves participants in shaping the impact of AI. Eligible Issue Areas The Open Call focuses on three key issue areas. 1. Education The education component supports efforts to shape AI around the interests of students, educators, and communities. Projects may focus on developing and expanding knowledge, strengthening how people learn, and safeguarding people against risks associated with AI. Humanity AI is particularly interested in work led by students, educators, and organizations representing them . 2. Labor and Economy The labor and economy area focuses on ensuring that AI enhances rather than simply replaces workers. The initiative seeks efforts that help create an economy where people can thrive and benefit from technological developments. Humanity AI is particularly interested in work led by workers and worker-focused organizations . 3. Humanities, Arts, and Culture The third issue area focuses on enhancing human creativity and understanding of the human experience while protecting artists and creators. Humanity AI is particularly interested in projects led by: Artists Writers Scholars Cultural heritage workers Other people working in culture and humanities Organizations representing these communities Eligible Approaches Within the three issue areas, Humanity AI is funding community-led work that follows one of three approaches. 1. Shaping How AI Is Governed and Used This approach supports efforts by communities and advocates to strengthen safeguards around AI and help define the rules governing AI deployment at local, regional, or national levels. Examples could include educators establishing AI guidelines for schools or workers organizing around enforceable standards for responsible AI use in the workplace. 2. Building AI on Community Terms This approach supports technical efforts that place community needs ahead of profits and focus on developing AI systems and infrastructure that communities can shape and control. Examples include: Evaluations centred on overlooked communities Auditing approaches to ensure AI systems work as intended Datasets supporting broad and consensual participation in AI development Artistic and creative approaches to community-led AI infrastructure Projects that reimagine, audit, or challenge AI systems Humanity AI prioritizes technical proposals focused on AI infrastructure . AI products using novel approaches may also be considered when they address a community gap and are co-designed with the communities they serve. 3. Challenging AI That Doesn t Serve Communities This approach supports community efforts to challenge AI deployments that are imposed on communities or do not align with their values and needs. The goal is to elevate approaches that place human agency at the centre of decision-making about AI. Examples include artists and cultural organizations using creative interventions to challenge dominant narratives about AI, or worker coalitions challenging AI surveillance in workplaces. Priority Consideration for Open-Weight and Open-Source AI Projects can be eligible whether or not they incorporate AI. However, when AI models are central to the proposed methodology or deliverables, priority will be given to open-weight and/or open-source models rather than closed models . Areas Out of Scope Applicants should carefully consider whether their proposed project falls within the scope of the Open Call. The following areas are specifically excluded: AI Literacy Projects primarily focused on providing people with knowledge and skills to use AI tools are out of scope. AI Adoption Projects primarily focused on promoting the spread of particular AI tools or systems are not eligible. Research-Only Projects Projects primarily focused on research without advancing community leadership and action are also out of scope. Eligibility Requirements The Humanity AI Open Call welcomes applications from: U.S.-based organizations U.S.-based collaborations U.S.-based individuals with eligible proposals focused on U.S.-based communities Lead organizations must have 501(c)(3) status . Individuals can apply with the support of a fiscal sponsor or another 501(c)(3) intermediary . Applicants based outside the United States should carefully review the official FAQ and eligibility requirements before preparing an application, as the call specifically states that applicants and proposed work must meet the U.S.-based requirements. Funding Amount Humanity AI will provide grants ranging from $75,000 to $1,000,000 . Applicants can select the funding tier that best matches the resources required for their proposal. Tier One: $75,000–$150,000 This tier may be suitable for: A fiscally sponsored project involving an individual practitioner A focused proposal A two-partner collaboration undertaking exploratory work An emerging organization launching an early initiative An established organization running a contained pilot Tier Two: $150,000–$500,000 This tier may be suitable for projects involving: Individual practitioners whose work requires sustained time or production resources Collaborations requiring meaningful coordination or development costs Emerging organizations with full-time teams working on defined initiatives Established organizations dedicating staff capacity to a new area of work Tier Three: $500,000–$1,000,000 This tier may be suitable for: Coalitions requiring substantial coordination and dedicated staffing Multi-year initiatives with significant technical development or infrastructure costs Emerging organizations building full-time teams around major initiatives Established organizations launching ambitious, resource-intensive pilots Humanity AI is not pre-allocating funding between the tiers. Applicants are encouraged to request the level of funding their proposal actually requires. Grant Duration Applicants may propose projects lasting up to three years . Where feasible, grants will be disbursed at the beginning of the grant period to support early resourcing. Application Process The application process consists of two phases. Phase 1: Initial Application Eligible applicants must submit their initial application by: October 21, 2026, at 4:59 p.m. PT / 7:59 p.m. ET. Applications will first undergo an eligibility screening by reviewers at Lever for Change, which is supporting the Open Call. Eligible applications will then be evaluated according to the Open Call s evaluation criteria. Phase 2: Finalist Round Top-rated applicants will be invited to submit additional application materials. These materials may include: A detailed budget A measurement plan Additional information about the proposed work Some applicants may also be invited to participate in an interview with Humanity AI staff and funders. Application Timeline September 10, 2026 Launch Initial applications opened. September 14, 2026 Applicant Webinar An informational webinar is scheduled for prospective applicants. October 21, 2026 Initial Applications Due Applications must be submitted by 4:59 p.m. PT / 7:59 p.m. ET . December 2026 Finalists Notified Finalists will be contacted and invited to provide additional materials. Early Spring 2027 Grantee Awards Announced Humanity AI expects to announce the successful grantee awards. The dates are estimates and may change. Humanity AI states that updates will be communicated as early as possible. Evaluation Criteria Proposals will be evaluated according to five major criteria: Vision for the Proposal Vision for Community Leadership Clarity and Feasibility Potential for Impact Credibility and Experience Applicants should therefore ensure that their proposals clearly communicate their vision, demonstrate meaningful community leadership, explain how the project can realistically be delivered, describe its potential impact, and establish the credibility and experience of those involved. How to Apply Prospective applicants are encouraged to begin by reviewing the organizational readiness tool to assess their eligibility. Applicants can also review the complete list of application questions before submitting their proposal. Start Application: Humanity AI Open Call application portal Assess Eligibility: Humanity AI organizational readiness tool Download Questions: Humanity AI Open Call application questions Who Should Consider Applying? This Open Call is particularly relevant to U.S.-based organizations, collaborations, and eligible individuals working with U.S.-based communities on projects involving: Education and AI Labor and the future of work Humanities, arts, and culture AI governance Community-led AI infrastructure Open-source or open-weight AI Community-led challenges to harmful AI deployment Human-centred approaches to AI development and use The strongest fit will be projects where affected communities are not merely consulted but are actively defining the goals, shaping the approach, and leading the work. Important Information for Applicants Before applying, prospective applicants should carefully assess whether their project meets the Open Call s requirements. Applicants should pay particular attention to: U.S.-based eligibility requirements 501(c)(3) requirements for lead organizations The need for a fiscal sponsor for eligible individual applicants The three eligible issue areas The three eligible approaches Areas that are specifically out of scope The preference for open-weight and open-source AI when AI models form part of the core methodology or deliverables The appropriate funding tier The maximum three-year grant duration The October 21, 2026 application deadline APPLICATION PORTAL APPLY HERE Conclusion The Humanity AI Open Call 2026 provides a major funding opportunity for U.S.-based communities, organizations, collaborations, and eligible individuals working to shape the development, governance, and use of artificial intelligence. With grants ranging from $75,000 to $1 million and project durations of up to three years, the initiative is designed to support community-led efforts across education, labor and the economy, and humanities, arts, and culture. Applicants should ensure that their proposals place communities at the centre of the work and clearly demonstrate a strong vision, community leadership, feasibility, potential impact, and relevant experience. title: 2027 Amelia Earhart Fellowship: US$12,000 Funding for Women Pursuing PhD Research in Aerospace Engineering and Space Sciences
summary: The 2027 Amelia Earhart Fellowship is now accepting applications from outstanding women pursuing doctoral-level studies and research in aerospace engineering and space sciences . Offered by Zonta International , the prestigious fellowship provides financial support to women who are advancing knowledge, innovation, exploration and research in some of the world s most competitive scientific and technological fields. Up to 30 women will be selected as 2027 Amelia Earhart Fellows , with each recipient receiving a US$12,000 fellowship to support their advanced doctoral studies. Established in 1938 in honor of renowned aviator and Zontian Amelia Earhart , the fellowship has a long history of supporting women who are breaking barriers in aerospace-related disciplines and developing the knowledge and technologies that shape the future of aviation, space exploration and science. The 2027 Amelia Earhart Fellowship application deadline is 15 November 2026 . About the Amelia Earhart Fellowship Women have made important contributions to aerospace engineering, aviation, astronomy, space exploration and other scientific fields. However, they remain significantly underrepresented in many areas of aerospace engineering and space sciences. The Amelia Earhart Fellowship was created to help address this imbalance by providing talented women with financial resources to continue advanced research and doctoral studies. For almost 90 years, Zonta International has supported women who are pursuing ambitious academic and professional goals. The fellowship specifically recognizes women whose doctoral research is applied to aerospace engineering or space sciences . The fellowship reflects Amelia Earhart s pioneering spirit and Zonta International s commitment to helping women gain access to the resources and opportunities necessary to become leaders and decision-makers in highly competitive fields. For the 2027 fellowship cycle: Up to 30 Fellows will be selected. Each Fellow will receive US$12,000 . The fellowship can support doctoral studies at an accredited university or college offering postgraduate courses and degrees in the relevant fields. Applicants can be studying at eligible institutions in different countries around the world. The program is designed specifically for women pursuing doctoral-level research connected to aerospace engineering or space sciences. What Makes the Amelia Earhart Fellowship Prestigious? The Amelia Earhart Fellowship has an extensive history of supporting women in aerospace and space-related disciplines. Since the program began, Zonta International has awarded: 1,824 Amelia Earhart Fellowships More than US$12.5 million in fellowship funding Support to 1,395 women Recipients from 81 countries Past Amelia Earhart Fellows have gone on to build influential careers in a wide range of fields. Alumnae have become: Astronauts Aerospace engineers Astronomers Professors Geologists Entrepreneurs Corporate leaders Senior public officials One former Fellow even went on to become the U.S. Secretary of the Air Force . These achievements demonstrate the potential impact of investing in women conducting advanced research in aerospace engineering and space sciences. 2027 Amelia Earhart Fellowship Funding Each selected Fellow will receive US$12,000 . The award is intended to provide financial support for eligible doctoral studies and research in aerospace engineering and space sciences. The fellowships are made possible through generous contributions to the Zonta Foundation for Women Amelia Earhart Fellowship Fund . The funding can therefore provide valuable financial assistance to doctoral researchers who are already undertaking advanced academic work and need additional resources to continue developing their research. Eligibility Requirements The Amelia Earhart Fellowship has specific academic and enrollment requirements. Applicants must meet the following requirements: 1. Applicants must be women The fellowship is specifically designed to support women pursuing advanced studies and research in aerospace engineering and space sciences. 2. Applicants may be of any nationality The fellowship is open to women of any nationality who satisfy the academic and program requirements. This means the opportunity is not restricted to applicants from a particular country or continent. 3. Applicants must be pursuing a Ph.D. or doctoral degree Applicants must be actively pursuing a Ph.D. or other doctoral degree . The doctoral program must involve research applied to aerospace engineering or space sciences . 4. Applicants must demonstrate a superior academic record Candidates are expected to demonstrate strong academic performance and evidence of excellence in their field. A competitive applicant should therefore be able to demonstrate a strong academic background alongside significant potential in aerospace engineering or space sciences. 5. Applicants must be conducting aerospace- or space-science-related research The applicant s research must be applied to: Aerospace engineering; or Space sciences. Applicants whose doctoral research falls outside these areas would not meet the central academic focus of the fellowship. 6. Applicants must be registered in a full-time doctoral program Applicants must be registered in a full-time Ph.D. or doctoral program . Part-time doctoral study does not satisfy this requirement. 7. Applicants must have completed at least one year of their doctoral program At the time of submitting the application, applicants must have either: Completed at least one year of their Ph.D./doctoral program ; or Received a master s degree in an aerospace-applied field . This requirement is important because the fellowship is intended for researchers who have already progressed beyond the very beginning of their advanced academic journey. 8. Applicants must not graduate before April 2028 Applicants must remain enrolled in their doctoral program long enough to meet the fellowship s timing requirements. Specifically, applicants must not graduate from their Ph.D. or doctoral program before April 2028 . Candidates whose doctoral studies are scheduled to end before this date are therefore not eligible for the 2027 fellowship. Who Is Not Eligible? Certain individuals are specifically excluded from applying. The following people are not eligible: Zonta club members Individuals with direct membership with Zonta International Employees of Zonta International Employees of the Zonta Foundation for Women Applicants participating in post-doctoral research programs Previous Amelia Earhart Fellows applying to renew the fellowship for a second year Applicants should carefully review their status before beginning the application process. Previous Amelia Earhart Fellows Previous recipients of the Amelia Earhart Fellowship cannot apply to renew the fellowship for a second year. However, Zonta notes that recipients of another Zonta fellowship or award who received a complimentary one-year supporting membership from Zonta International may still be eligible to apply during that complimentary membership year, provided they are not applying for the same fellowship or scholarship they previously received from Zonta International . The Sharon Langenbeck Amelia Earhart Fellow A special distinction has been introduced within the Amelia Earhart Fellowship program. In 2025, Sharon Langenbeck, Ph.D. , a Past International President and a two-time Amelia Earhart Fellow from 1977 and 1978, made an extraordinary contribution to the Amelia Earhart Endowment Fund. In recognition of her generosity and lasting contribution to the fellowship program, one of the 30 Amelia Earhart Fellows selected each year will be designated the Sharon Langenbeck Amelia Earhart Fellow . The Fellow will be selected by the Zonta International Amelia Earhart Committee according to pre-established criteria. Sharon Langenbeck continues to support the legacy of Amelia Earhart and the women following in her footsteps. From 2026 to 2028 , she is also serving as the Amelia Earhart Fellowship 90th Anniversary Ambassador . This role forms part of Zonta International s preparations to celebrate the fellowship s 90th anniversary during the 2026–2028 Biennium . How the Application Is Evaluated Applications are reviewed by the Zonta International Amelia Earhart Fellowship Committee . The committee reviews submitted applications and recommends selected recipients to the Zonta International Board . Applicants are evaluated according to the criteria established in the fellowship requirements and application. The evaluation process is confidential. Zonta International states that: Application evaluations are kept confidential. Evaluations are not disclosed to applicants. Applicants will be notified of their application status by the end of April . Because the fellowship is highly competitive, prospective applicants should ensure that their application clearly demonstrates their academic excellence, doctoral progress and relevance of their research to aerospace engineering or space sciences. Application Deadline The deadline for the 2027 Amelia Earhart Fellowship is: 15 November 2026 The complete application must be submitted by this date to be considered. Applicants should avoid waiting until the final day to submit their applications. Preparing an application for a highly competitive doctoral fellowship may require sufficient time to gather academic information and prepare the required supporting materials. Where Can Applicants Come From? The Amelia Earhart Fellowship is open to women of any nationality . The program s history demonstrates its international reach, with previous Fellows coming from 81 countries . Therefore, eligible applicants can come from different countries and continents, including applicants from Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, South America, Oceania and other regions , provided they satisfy all of the fellowship s academic, doctoral-program and research requirements. For example, an eligible woman pursuing a qualifying Ph.D. in Ghana or another African country can potentially apply, provided that she meets all of the stated requirements. Nationality alone does not determine eligibility; the applicant s doctoral program, research area, academic record and stage of study are particularly important. Who Should Apply? The fellowship is particularly relevant to women who are already undertaking advanced doctoral research in areas such as: Aerospace engineering Space sciences Aviation-related engineering research Astronomical research Space exploration technologies Aerospace systems Other doctoral research directly applied to aerospace engineering or space sciences Applicants should carefully determine whether their specific research topic falls within the fellowship s scope before submitting an application. Why This Fellowship Matters The Amelia Earhart Fellowship offers more than financial assistance. For doctoral researchers, receiving a prestigious international fellowship can provide recognition of their academic achievements and research potential. The opportunity can help women: Receive financial support The US$12,000 fellowship can help support advanced doctoral studies and research. Gain international recognition Becoming an Amelia Earhart Fellow places a researcher within a distinguished international network of women working in aerospace and space sciences. Strengthen their academic profile A competitive international fellowship can become a valuable addition to an academic CV and professional profile. Join a distinguished fellowship legacy Fellows become part of a program that has supported women for almost nine decades. Connect with an international community The program s history includes Fellows from 81 countries, creating a broad international legacy. Advance research in cutting-edge fields Successful applicants are contributing to scientific and technological developments in aerospace engineering and space sciences. Develop future leadership opportunities Former Fellows have progressed into influential careers as scientists, engineers, academics, entrepreneurs, corporate leaders and public officials. 2026 Amelia Earhart Fellows The 2026 cohort demonstrates the international nature of the fellowship. The 2026 Amelia Earhart Fellows include women from countries and territories such as: India United States Canada Democratic Republic of Congo Italy Ireland United Kingdom South Korea Thailand Hong Kong and China China The 2026 cohort includes 30 Fellows , one of whom was designated the 2026 Sharon Langenbeck Amelia Earhart Fellow . This international representation highlights the fellowship s commitment to supporting talented women regardless of nationality. Program Documents and Additional Information Zonta International provides several documents relating to the Amelia Earhart Fellowship. Prospective applicants can consult the available program materials for additional information, including: 2026 Amelia Earhart Fellows 2026 Amelia Earhart Fellows biographies Amelia Earhart Fellowship Map Amelia Earhart Fellowship School List Amelia Earhart Fellowship Statistics and Program Overview Amelia Earhart Fellowship Description These materials can help prospective applicants understand the fellowship s history, previous recipients, participating institutions and overall program structure. Important Things Applicants Should Remember Before applying, prospective candidates should carefully check that they satisfy the major requirements. In particular, applicants should confirm that: They are women. They are of any nationality and meet the program requirements. They are pursuing a Ph.D. or doctoral degree. Their research is applied to aerospace engineering or space sciences. They are enrolled in a full-time doctoral program. They have completed at least one year of the doctoral program, or have a master s degree in an aerospace-applied field. They will not graduate from their doctoral program before April 2028. title: Skills & Innovation Academy Ghana 2026: GIZ Opens 5-Day Employability Training for Graduates in Greater Accra, Bono, Northern and Upper West
summary: Applications are now open for the Skills Innovation Academy 2026 , an intensive five-day professional development programme designed to help graduates strengthen their technical and soft skills and improve their readiness for the world of work. The current application round targets graduates based in four regions of Ghana: Greater Accra Bono Northern Region Upper West Region The Academy is an initiative of Invest for Jobs – Special Initiative “Decent Work for a Just Transition” , an initiative of Germany’s Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) and implemented by the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH . GIZ Ghana’s current call describes the programme as an intensive five-day technical and soft-skills training aimed at improving participants’ employability. The application deadline is: 23 September 2026 Interested candidates can submit their applications through the official registration form. Apply for the Skills Innovation Academy 2026 About the Skills Innovation Academy The Skills Innovation Academy is a short, intensive employability training initiative designed to help graduates strengthen the practical skills needed to transition more effectively into employment. The current September 2026 call invites graduates from Greater Accra, Bono, Northern and Upper West who want to upgrade their skills and improve their employability. Participants will take part in five days of technical and soft-skills training focused on preparing them for the demands of the workplace. The programme is particularly relevant to graduates who may already have academic qualifications but want additional practical preparation before entering or progressing in the labour market. It reflects a wider challenge facing many young graduates: completing formal education does not always mean that a person has had sufficient opportunities to develop the practical, interpersonal and workplace skills employers expect. The Academy therefore seeks to help bridge the space between: Academic learning and employment Technical knowledge and workplace application Qualifications and job readiness Graduate potential and employer expectations Who Is Behind the Skills Innovation Academy? The Academy is linked to Invest for Jobs – Special Initiative “Decent Work for a Just Transition.” The initiative is supported by the Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development of Germany, BMZ , and implemented by GIZ . The current call was published by GIZ Ghana. GIZ is Germany’s international cooperation agency and works with governments, private-sector institutions, civil society and other partners on programmes connected to areas such as: Employment Economic development Skills Governance Sustainability Private-sector development Innovation Within Ghana, the Skills Innovation Academy fits particularly closely with employment and workforce-development objectives. What Is Invest for Jobs? Invest for Jobs is associated with the German development cooperation initiative focused on supporting decent employment and sustainable economic development . For graduates, programmes supported under this framework may be particularly valuable because they focus not only on education in the abstract, but on the transition into actual economic and professional opportunities. The Skills Innovation Academy therefore emphasizes practical preparation for work rather than purely academic instruction. What Does the Programme Offer? The current call describes the Academy as an: Intensive 5-day technical and soft-skills training programme. Its central objective is to equip participants with practical skills that can help them function more effectively in the workplace and compete for employment opportunities. The programme combines two broad areas: 1. Technical Skills Technical skills are the practical or job-related capabilities people need to perform professional tasks. The exact technical modules for the September 2026 cohort are not listed in the public announcement provided by GIZ Ghana. Applicants should therefore avoid assuming that a specific technology, profession or vocational field is guaranteed unless it is stated in the registration form or communicated directly by programme organizers. The important point from the current call is that technical training forms part of the five-day programme. 2. Soft Skills Soft skills refer to the interpersonal and professional behaviours that help employees function successfully in organizations. These can generally relate to areas such as: Communication Teamwork Professionalism Problem-solving Workplace behaviour Adaptability Collaboration Self-management However, the current public call does not publish a detailed list of the September cohort’s exact soft-skills modules. Applicants should therefore rely on the current registration materials for the definitive curriculum. Why Soft Skills Matter for Graduates Employers often evaluate candidates on more than academic qualifications. A graduate may have strong academic knowledge but still need to develop the ability to: Communicate clearly Collaborate with colleagues Manage responsibilities Present ideas professionally Adapt to workplace expectations Solve practical problems Demonstrate initiative This is one reason short employability programmes can be useful during the transition between education and work. The Skills Innovation Academy specifically positions itself around strengthening employability through both technical and interpersonal development. The Academy Is Focused on Practical Employability The wording of the current call is important. GIZ Ghana does not describe this as a theoretical academic course. It says the training is intended to equip participants with practical skills for the world of work . That means the Academy should be particularly relevant to individuals who want to become more workplace-ready. Potential participants may include graduates who are: Searching for their first job Preparing for employment Trying to strengthen their professional profile Looking to build practical skills after graduation Seeking to improve confidence in professional environments Preparing to transition into a new career area Programme Duration The Skills Innovation Academy lasts: Five days The training is described as intensive, meaning participants should expect a concentrated learning schedule rather than a long-term part-time programme. Applicants should ensure that they can commit to the programme once selected. The current public announcement does not specify the exact training dates or daily schedule, so selected participants should rely on instructions from GIZ or the implementing team. Is This a Job? No. The Skills Innovation Academy is a training and employability development programme . Applicants should not interpret participation as: A job offer Guaranteed employment An internship A paid position Its purpose is to strengthen participants’ skills and employability. The public call does not state that completion automatically results in placement with an employer. Is This a Scholarship? No. The opportunity is not advertised as an academic scholarship. Participants are not applying for: University tuition A degree Research funding Academic study abroad Instead, they are applying for a short professional skills-development programme. Is There a Stipend or Financial Allowance? The current September 2026 public call does not state that participants will receive a stipend, transport allowance, accommodation allowance or cash payment . It also does not publicly specify: Training fee Accommodation provision Meals Transport support Certificate Employment guarantee Applicants should therefore avoid assuming that these benefits are included unless the registration form or organizers confirm them. This is especially important when promoting the opportunity: it should not be described as “fully funded” based solely on the currently published announcement. Current Target Regions The September 2026 call specifically targets graduates in: Greater Accra Greater Accra is Ghana’s main administrative and economic centre and includes Accra and its surrounding metropolitan areas. Graduates living in this region form one of the target groups for the current round. Bono Region Graduates in the Bono Region are also invited to participate. Northern Region The current programme expands access to graduates in Northern Ghana through inclusion of the Northern Region. Upper West Region Graduates based in Upper West are also among the target participants. The geographical targeting is therefore not nationwide in the current announcement. A Region-Based Programme Model The Skills Innovation Academy appears to use different regional application rounds. For example, an earlier GIZ Ghana round in June 2026 targeted applicants in: Greater Accra Eastern Region Volta Region and described eligibility for that particular round as SHS graduate or higher . The current September round is different: it specifically names: Greater Accra Bono Northern Upper West and simply refers to applicants as graduates . Applicants should therefore follow the requirements of the current September 2026 call , rather than assuming that every criterion from an earlier regional round automatically applies. What Academic Qualification Is Required? The current public announcement asks: “Are you a graduate in the Greater Accra, Bono, Northern Upper West…” However, it does not publicly define the precise educational level meant by “graduate” in the current call. For example, the announcement does not explicitly state whether the September round requires: SHS completion Diploma HND Bachelor’s degree University degree Any post-secondary qualification An earlier 2026 round explicitly said SHS graduate or higher , but the current September announcement does not repeat that exact wording. Therefore, applicants should complete the official form and follow the current eligibility questions rather than assuming a specific tertiary degree is compulsory. Is There an Age Limit? The current Skills Innovation Academy announcement does not state an age limit . It does not publicly specify: Minimum age Maximum age A youth age bracket such as 18–35 Therefore, an age restriction should not be added to promotional material unless it appears in the current application form. Is Work Experience Required? The current call does not state a minimum work-experience requirement. Applicants are therefore not publicly required to have: One year of experience Two years of experience Prior professional employment Previous internship experience The programme is presented around strengthening graduate employability, which suggests that it is particularly relevant to people at an early stage of their careers. What Fields of Study Can Apply? The current announcement does not restrict participation to one academic field. It does not state that candidates must be graduates of: STEM Business Engineering IT Humanities Social sciences or another specific discipline. The wording is broad: graduates seeking to improve their skills and employability . Applicants from different academic backgrounds may therefore consider applying, unless the registration form contains additional track-specific requirements. What Participants Could Gain Although the current call does not publish an exhaustive list of outputs, the programme is designed to improve participants’ readiness for employment. Potential professional value includes: Stronger Workplace Skills Participants can develop a better understanding of the behaviours and practical abilities needed in professional environments. Improved Technical Capacity The programme includes technical-skills training alongside soft skills. Greater Employability The Academy is explicitly marketed as an opportunity to upgrade skills and improve employability. Professional Development A concentrated skills programme can help graduates identify areas requiring further development before applying for jobs. Why Employability Training Matters The transition from education into employment can be difficult, particularly where graduates have limited opportunities to gain workplace experience. Common challenges can include: Limited practical experience Lack of familiarity with workplace expectations Difficulty translating qualifications into job-ready skills Weak interview preparation Limited professional networks Insufficient soft-skills training Programmes such as the Skills Innovation Academy seek to strengthen the practical side of graduate preparation. How to Apply Applications are submitted through the official online registration form. The public call also notes that applicants can register through the QR code displayed on the programme flyer. Application Deadline The deadline is: 23 September 2026 GIZ Ghana’s current public announcement confirms this closing date. Applicants should consider submitting early in case they experience: Connectivity problems Form errors Missing documents Last-minute technical difficulties How to Prepare Before Applying 1. Review Your Educational Information Have accurate details of your: Educational institution Qualification Field of study Graduation status ready before beginning. 2. Be Clear About Your Employment Goals If the form asks why you want to join, avoid generic answers such as: “I want to gain skills.” Instead explain: What career area you want to enter What skills you currently lack Why the programme would help you How you intend to use the training 3. Explain Your Employability Gap A strong response might identify a practical challenge such as: Limited professional experience Weak digital skills Limited workplace exposure Need for stronger communication skills Difficulty transitioning from school to employment Then explain how training could help address it. 4. Who Should Consider Applying? This opportunity may be especially relevant if you: Have recently graduated Are searching for employment Want to strengthen your practical skills Want stronger workplace readiness Live in one of the targeted regions Can commit to an intensive five-day programme Key Information at a Glance Programme: Skills Innovation Academy 2026 Country: Ghana Organizer/Implementer: GIZ Ghana Initiative: Invest for Jobs – Special Initiative “Decent Work for a Just Transition” Supporting ministry: German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ) Duration: 5 days Training focus: Technical and soft skills Purpose: Improve practical skills and employability Target participants: Graduates Regions: Greater Accra, Bono, Northern and Upper West Deadline: 23 September 2026 Application method: Online registration Application link: Skills Innovation Academy registration form The current call does not publicly state a stipend, job guarantee, accommodation package, participation allowance, age restriction or precise academic degree threshold. Conclusion The Skills Innovation Academy Ghana 2026 offers graduates in Greater Accra, Bono, Northern and Upper West an opportunity to spend five intensive days strengthening practical technical and soft skills for the workplace. The programme is part of Invest for Jobs – Special Initiative “Decent Work for a Just Transition,” supported by Germany’s BMZ and implemented by GIZ . Its emphasis is firmly on employability: helping graduates strengthen the competencies needed to transition more effectively from education into professional environments. The current call does not promise employment, a stipend or an internship. It should instead be understood as a short professional-development and skills-training opportunity. Applicants should also pay attention to the regional eligibility. The September 2026 round specifically names graduates located in Greater Accra, Bono, Northern and Upper West , and should not automatically be promoted as open to every region of Ghana.
